 ],
 "search_notes": "METHOD. 16 WebSearch queries (mechfight bot github; mech royale buildathon; \"mechfight/1\"; Builders Buildathon + Mech Royale; mechfight.py Dockerfile; joinbuilders; mech-royale-bot; leaderboard team names in three batches; LanceHuang245; oval; house bots weakest first; site:github.com variants). General web search is nearly blind to this one-day-old event (one extended site:github.com query returned 10 repos). Discovery therefore relied on ~50 GitHub repository searches through gh (names, descriptions, in:readme for mechfight / mech royale / mechfight-kit / joinbuilders, created-time slices), giving ~130 Mech Royale repos. README files of 103 were fetched read-only for triage; 31 repos were shallow-cloned one at a time with the mandated command into P/intel/<owner>__<repo>. Triage files are in P/intel/_triage (cands_f.tsv = candidate list, readme/ = fetched READMEs, raw/ = three historical files fetched by commit). Nothing was executed, nothing copied into bot/sim/tools/notes. GitHub REST API calls for forks/user listings are blocked in this session, so fork lists were not checked.\n\nTEAM-TO-REPO MAP. Wolverines = varchaskukreja/TTUN (confirmed by r1ver's notes). r1ver = moonriver0922/wgsrobot. BackwardsDeployeds = brycehcmcgrath/mechfight-bot. Kanyaraasi = devakchow/team-kanyaraasi-mech-royale (LanceHuang245 commit 171bc06 with quiet movement disabled and one small retreat tweak; no new ideas). AT: not confirmed; anthonyteti/buildathon-mech-royale is a guess from initials. BobBuildIt: not confirmed; VivekRnx/bob-the-builder-2026 and Osca-K/builders-buildit-mech-royale have similar names but claim no score. No public repo found for A-bot LLC, tigerbyte, ImagineLosing, \"not even close\", Mahalas, Mustikas, TigerTown27, Antalos, 314159265.\n\nLEADERBOARD TIMELINE (from competitors' logs, Eastern time Fri Nov 20): 21:00 top 5.23 of 94 teams; 21:40 AT 5.40, 16th 4.33, 32nd 4.04, median 3.53 of 108; ~22:00 AT 5.48, BobBuildIt 5.25, Wolverines 5.19, r1ver 5.08-5.10; 23:17 1st 5.58, 16th 4.73, 32nd 4.23; 23:48 1st 5.58, 16th 4.77, 32nd 4.29 of 144. The cutoff is rising about 0.05-0.1 per hour.\n\nCROSS-REPO FINDINGS MEASURED ON THE OFFICIAL SCORER.\n1. Scoring replays the same 48 seeds: identical code gives an identical score (four teams confirmed). Any behaviour change re-rolls matches; one team measured ~0.06 from an RNG salt alone, another saw 3.75 vs 3.90 for one version (wall-clock-dependent planning). Treat deltas under ~0.2 as noise. Per-match results are bimodal (mostly 0-2 or 15), so the mean is driven by how often the bot wins outright.\n2. Passivity loses in practice: hide-and-hold-fire 4.04 vs 4.54; idle regen while unseen -0.44; quiet walking -0.2 (4.54 vs 4.75; 4.54 vs 4.67); rooftop camping 3.23 vs 3.60; roof fighting and long-range fighting 'scored worse' (BingBU); long-range kiting -0.77; long-range gun+laser stack -0.46; combined caution 2.69 vs 3.29; holding behind cover -0.15. Faster strafe reversals -0.7 in one test.\n3. What gained: engaging mechs that shoot/aim at us instead of every mech +0.23 (one team; Wolverines at 5.19 fight everything tracked, so this is not universal); targets the current burst can finish +0.39; cube/upgrade-value economy (Wolverines 5.19, r1ver 5.08-5.10); supply drops chased to 300 m +0.02; break line of sight when hurt/outnumbered then re-engage +0.14; execution fixes (trigger held across cooldown end, LOS-aware aim point).\n4. Consensus loadout: laser + lightning, mortar skipped; lightning fights at ~28-30 m, laser ~110 m, gun 70-100 m; upgrades plating/armor/nanites first.\n5. Free-for-all detection used by at least six teams: deaths not caused by us (alive count drop minus own kills >= 2-3) or beams ending on other mechs; practice house bots never trigger it. Top practice bots placed only 6th-12th in the Top-16 showdown; calm, well-cubed bots and expert house bots did best there.\n6. Local simulators do not rank tactics reliably (r1ver 3 of 6 orderings right; nullat0m7 and jackbalseca sims predicted gains for changes that lost 0.46-0.77). Real house bots hunt a passive bot less aggressively than sims assume.\n7. Real-engine testing exists: several teams bridge their bot to private rooms on the public play server play.joinbuilders.org (room code from its matchmaking endpoint; empty seats are server house bots) and record the public cast websocket at watch.joinbuilders.org/live. Tools for this are in jklein07/mech-royale-bot, micah-andelman/mech-royale (also emulates a practice squad with 15 vision-sharing hunter clients), Achintya-Lakshmanan and jackbalseca. This needs outbound network and was not tried here.\n\nOTHER REPOS READ BUT NOT RANKED. niranjankumarnk/mech-royale (BingBU, Rust, policy switches; roof and long-range variants kept off after scoring worse); micah-andelman/mech-royale (own Python brain, lists which teams' ideas it reimplemented); jklein07/mech-royale-bot (Rust, large sim, house aim notes); Warrior-hound/mech-royale (hit-probability fire gate, time-to-kill engagement gate, 37-spot hide search; sim only); koillea/mech-royale-goonies (roof perch catalogue and climb procedure; no score); VivekRnx/bob-the-builder-2026 (sim + browser replay viewer; sim-only numbers); AbhirajTiwari12/mech-royale-bot (89 KB bot, quiet loot-first opening, no score); viktor-lorentz/mech-royale-overcooked (Rust sim with house calibration); Borovail/builders-mech-royale (score calibration CSVs, own scores 1.56-2.0); ppetit8 (2.50/3.27/3.46); Sharmileer 2.58; akshayagg18 2.48; Rebecca922 2.06; afiapoks 1.38; kpfarn 0.13 and 0.06 with pure stealth (hiding without fighting scores near zero); whyMiso (claimed 4.13 elsewhere, repo now holds only a README). davidvarvas x2, gonvaz-nocode/NoCodeHack, bzells11, suzhuhui-hub/oval-warden, OvitasO: original bots without score claims.\n\nCAVEATS. Scores are self-reported in READMEs/logs or relayed by other teams; none were verified against the official board. Several top entries are derivatives of the MIT-licensed LanceHuang245 and TTUN bots, so 'top entries are compared' will cluster around those two code bases; our own implementation should stay clearly distinct."
